topic: Instantaneous Rate of Change and the Derivative

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Average Rate of Change
sections.content: Define average rate of change as the slope of a secant line between two points (x, f(x)) and (x+h, f(x+h)). Use a visual of a car traveling between two points on a road to show the concept of 'average speed'.
sections.example: A cheetah runs from point A to point B. Average speed = total distance / total time.

sections.title: The Conceptual Bridge: Shrinking the Interval
sections.content: Animate the second point moving closer to the first point (h approaches 0). Visually demonstrate how the secant line transforms into a tangent line. Introduce the concept that as 'h' gets smaller, the average rate of change approaches the 'instantaneous' rate.
sections.example: Visualize the cheetah's journey: instead of calculating speed over 1 hour, we calculate it over 1 minute, then 1 second, then a millisecond.

sections.title: Formal Definition: The Derivative
sections.content: Introduce the formal limit definition: f'(x) = lim(h→0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h. Explain this as the slope of the tangent line at a specific point, which represents the instantaneous rate of change.
sections.example: A motion tracker on the cheetah displaying the exact speedometer reading at the precise moment it reaches a specific tree.

sections.title: Application: Visualizing the Slope
sections.content: Show a graph of a non-linear function (a parabola). Move a tangent line along the curve, demonstrating how the slope (derivative value) changes dynamically. This connects algebraic limits to geometric reality.
sections.example: A drone pilot monitoring the climb rate of their craft; the derivative is the real-time vertical speed shown on the controller display.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
sections.content: Recap: Derivative = slope of the tangent = instantaneous rate of change. Remind students that the derivative is the 'limit' of the average rate of change as the interval disappears.
sections.example: Final infographic comparing the 'average' (broad span) vs. the 'derivative' (the exact snapshot moment).
